pages.title: What Is Waste?
pages.content:
It is Saturday evening. Yusuf and his mother are in the kitchen. Yusuf helps her. There is some hard bread on the table. “Mom, this bread is hard. What can we do?” Yusuf asks.

His mother smiles. “Do not throw it away! It is not waste! We can make bread soup!” Yusuf is surprised. “What is waste, Mom?” he asks.

Mom laughs. “Waste is everything we throw away,” she says. “Hard bread, old boxes, bottles and bags. Every day, people throw away a lot of things. The bins in our city are full. But we can use many things again. Come here. Let’s look at our kitchen together.”

vocabulary.definition: Things we throw away.
Boxes for things we throw away.

pages.title: Paper and Glass
pages.content:
Yusuf looks at the table. There is an old box and an empty jar. “Are they waste, Mom?” he asks.

“No, Yusuf,” Mom says. “This box is paper. Paper comes from trees. We can recycle it. Then people make new paper from it. This jar is glass. We can use it again. We can put sugar in it. We can put flowers in it, too. Old glass can go in the glass bin. Then people make new bottles and jars from it.”

Yusuf puts the box in the paper bin. Mom washes the jar.

vocabulary.definition: A glass box for food, like sugar or jam.
Make new things from old things.
A hard material. You can see through it.

pages.title: Plastic and the Sea
pages.content:
Then Yusuf finds a plastic bottle. “And this, Mom?” he asks.

“Plastic is a big problem,” Mom says. “Some people throw plastic into rivers and the sea. Fish and birds eat it. Then they are very sick. The water is dirty, too. So, we put plastic in the plastic bin. We never throw it on the ground or in the sea.” Yusuf looks sad. “Poor fish!” he says. Then he puts the bottle in the plastic bin.

vocabulary.definition: A light material. Bottles and bags are made of it.

pages.title: Old Bread
pages.content: Mom says again, “A lot of food goes in the bin. It is a big problem. And where is the biggest problem? It is at home! We buy a lot of food. Then we can’t eat it all. So, we only buy the food we need. And we eat yesterday’s bread first.” Yusuf smiles. “I like bread soup!” he says.

vocabulary.definition: Things we eat.

pages.title: Old Batteries
pages.content:
Yusuf opens a drawer. There are some old batteries in it. “Can I put these in the bin, Mom?” he asks.

“No, Yusuf. Batteries are dangerous,” Mom says. “They can’t go in the kitchen bin. There is a battery bin at your school. Take them there.” Yusuf puts the batteries in his school bag. “And old phones?” he asks. “They go to a special bin, too,” Mom says. “People open them and take the good parts. They make new things with them.”

vocabulary.definition: Small things with power for phones and toys.
It can hurt you.

pages.title: The Three Rs
pages.content:
Yusuf looks at the bins. “Mom, is there zero waste in our house now?” he asks.

Mom laughs. “Zero Waste doesn’t mean ‘no waste,’ Yusuf. It means less waste. Remember the three Rs,” she says. “Reduce: use less. Reuse: use things again. Recycle: make new things from old things.” Yusuf shows three fingers. “Reduce, reuse, recycle!” he says.

The next day, they go to the shop. Yusuf takes his own bag. “No plastic bags today, Mom!” he says. Mom is very happy.

Use things again.
